newsitem.title: MEXICO: Latin American stk markets seen cautious, volatile.
newsitem.headline: Latin American stk markets seen cautious, volatile.

text.p: Latin American stock markets are seen facing a week of uncertainty and volatility.
Analysts said local issues would likely affect the markets, though few clear trends are evident.
In Mexico's stock market, share prices are expected to be influenced by caution among both local and foreign investors, as well as volatility in exchange and interest rates.
Morgan Stanley said in a report that the focus should start to shift to third-quarter earnings.
It said it expects solid third-quarter results in Mexico, "especially on a year/year cash earnings basis."
Brazilian shares were expected to show no clear trend during the week because of rising volatility, especially after futures settlements on Wednesday and ahead of next Monday's options expiry.
Brokers said electricity sector stocks, up strongly last week on favorable prospects for privatization, were seen rising further, but the outlook for other shares was less clear.
"There's no real trend," said Marco Sa of Banco Geral do Comercio. "Anything can happen."
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index .BVSP declined 0.2 percent last week to close at 66,087 points. So far this month, the Bovespa has risen 2.5 percent.
After rallying last week, Chilean blue chips were expected to hold steady this week with attention focused on the electricity and banking sectors, said traders.
"The market looks firm this week, although without any surprises," said Lance Eckel, an analyst at brokerage Sud Americano.
Electricity stocks, which account for a nearly 40 percent weighting in the selective IPSA index, are seen rising as many investors believe they are undervalued, said Eckel.
But other traders expect the power sector to show little change November, when the government will release new electricity tariffs, which are expected to be sharply lower than current prices.
The 40-share IPSA index ended last week up 1.22 percent at 102.25 points after profit-taking eroded strong gains seen earlier in the week.
Analysts said the medium-term outlook for the Argentine market remains favorable but they did not rule out the possibility of short-lived declines.
"There will be no strong corrections, just normal ones within a rising market," said Roberto Diaz, an analyst at Provincia Burstil.
Morgan Stanley analysts said they were unexcited about the Argentine market because of an unfavorable outlook for earnings growth.
"Our analysts expect disappointing results in most of the stocks we cover...," Morgan Stanley said.
The Wall Street brokerage and investment house said that disappointments were most likely in the telephone and banking sectors.
-- Robert Kozak, Mexico City newsroom (525) 728 9559
